item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antibiotic

lookback_source.quote: N0415F1. Antibiotic: Check if an antibiotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period (referred to elsewhere for N0415 as the "7-day observation period"), or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. The manual does not state on these pages how the 7 days are counted relative to the ARD.

coding_levels.label: Antibiotic — Is taking (Column 1)
coding_levels.definition: Check if an antibiotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415F1. Antibiotic: Check if an antibiotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Antibiotic — Indication noted (Column 2)
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all antibiotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415F2. Antibiotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antibiotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: None of the above

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 is coded only if Column 1 is checked; check Column 2 if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: The above resource list is not all-inclusive, and use of these resources is not required for MDS completion.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Stated as Step 1 for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Stated as Step 2 for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: An "indication" is the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals; Column 2 requires such an indication for all medications in the class.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box on the same page as the coding instructions.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding of pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used reference resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that the source is identifiable.

federal.criterion: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert for the medication's pharmacological classification and may work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm classification.

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415F (Antibiotic) to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Terminology for the N0415 window: "7-day look-back period" vs. "7-day observation period"

positions.claim: N0415F1 is described as covering the "7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: N0415F1. Antibiotic: Check if an antibiotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: The general N0415 Column 1 coding instruction describes the window as the "7-day observation period."

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Both passages describe a 7-day window; the differing labels appear to be used interchangeably in the manual. Terminology difference only — no substantive conflict identified in the document.
